title: Doing What Matters in Times of Stress: An Illustrated Guide
summary: A WHO illustrated guide introducing practical stress-coping techniques intended for people facing adversity. Its existence provides a resource pointer for self-help education, not evidence that TherapyBot can deliver an effective intervention.
limitations: Publication is an educational self-help resource; publisher describes field testing and evidence-informed design but does not validate this chatbot, a particular diagnosis, or the safety of unsupervised AI guidance.
rights: Bibliographic pointer and original paraphrase only; do not redistribute the guide or train on it without a separate rights assessment.
verification_method: Official WHO publication page inspected; date, title, format and scope directly verified 2026-11-04

title: Psychological self-help interventions: delivering self-help for individuals, featuring Step-by-Step and Doing What Matters in Times of Stress
summary: WHO guidance for programme managers and providers describes structured, guided and unguided psychological self-help interventions across formats and settings.
limitations: Claims of trial evidence concern WHO-described intervention programmes; they do not imply that a generic AI companion implements those programmes faithfully, is clinically effective, or can operate without governance.
rights: Metadata and original high-level paraphrase only; publication text, scripts and materials not copied or approved for training.
verification_method: Official WHO publication page overview, date, reference number and intended audience inspected 2026-11-04

title: Depression in children and young people: identification and management (NG134)
issuer: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
summary: NICE guidance addresses identification and treatment of depression in children and young people, including professional skill, care-context and social-factor considerations.
limitations: Recommendations are for appropriately trained health professionals, not a general-purpose chatbot. Consent, capacity, safeguarding and developmental context are important; direct NICE chapter retrieval returned 403 during this wave, so specific recommendations require a section-level verification pass.
rights: Only link and original metadata summary used; no guideline text copied for training or redistribution.
verification_method: Official NICE search-indexed page verified guideline ID and 2019-06-25 publication; full chapter direct fetch 403, so section-level detail unverified

title: Psychosocial interventions for self-harm in adults
summary: A Cochrane review assesses trial evidence on psychosocial interventions for adults who self-harm, including cognitive-behavioral approaches and other structured therapies.
limitations: Review estimates concern specified intervention protocols and enrolled adults, with outcome and bias limitations; it does not justify relying on keyword suicide-risk prediction or delivery of emergency care by TherapyBot.
rights: DOI pointer and original abstract-level paraphrase only; full review content and model-training rights not cleared.
authors: Witt KG, Hetrick SE, Rajaram G, Hazell P, Taylor Salisbury TL, Townsend E, Hawton K
verification_method: Cochrane publisher's official evidence summary verified DOI, exact authors and issue/date; source article abstract-level review, not full study extraction

title: Foundational helping skills training manual: a competency-based approach for training helpers to support adults
summary: WHO/UNICEF EQUIP guidance describes training and assessing foundational helping skills such as communication, empathy and collaboration among adults' helpers.
limitations: Designed for human trainers and supervisors with competency assessment; cannot be directly treated as an AI-model evaluation or evidence that model-generated empathy is reliably non-harmful.
rights: Link and original bibliographic paraphrase only; no manual or exercises reproduced, model training not authorized.
verification_method: Official WHO publisher page directly verified 2025-07-10 date, authors and intended trainers/supervisors

title: Ensuring Quality in Psychosocial and Mental Health Care (EQUIP): compendium of competency assessment tools
summary: A WHO/UNICEF EQUIP reference on competency assessment instruments, evidence background and use in supervised mental-health service training.
limitations: Instruments are designed for health-service workforces and may have human-rater assumptions; no direct evidence for using them as a stand-alone AI mental-health agent qualification rubric.
rights: Bibliographic metadata only; assessment tools and manual content not reproduced, training rights uncleared.
verification_method: Official WHO publisher record directly verified title, publication date and intended competency assessment scope

title: Cognitive behavioural therapy and third-wave approaches for anxiety and related disorders in older people
summary: A Cochrane synthesis of 21 randomized trials involving 1,234 adults aged 55 or older examined CBT and related approaches for anxiety disorders, finding possible post-treatment symptom reductions but uncertain long-term effects.
limitations: Review authors rated much evidence low certainty and noted heterogeneous trials, bias risks and limited comparisons with other therapies; it provides no evidence for an autonomous chatbot delivering CBT.
rights: Publisher citation metadata and independent paraphrase only; Cochrane review body not copied, training rights not assessed.
authors: Hendriks G-J, Janssen N, Robertson L, van Balkom AJ, van Zelst WH, Wolfe S, Oude Voshaar RC, Uphoff E
verification_method: Official Cochrane abstract and citation directly inspected; 21 trials, 1234 participants, DOI and 2024-07-08 date verified

title: Psychological first aid: Guide for field workers
issuer: World Health Organization, War Trauma Foundation and World Vision International
summary: A WHO-coordinated practical guide describes humane, supportive assistance after severe distressing events with attention to people's dignity, culture and abilities.
limitations: Developed for human responders and humanitarian contexts; not proof that automated advice can replace emergency services or professional clinical assessment.
rights: Citation and high-level paraphrase only; official 2011 PDF specifies permission requests for reproduction or translation; no text copied or model training authorized.
authors: World Health Organization, War Trauma Foundation and World Vision International
verification_method: Official WHO 2011 technical publication page inspected for date, authors, audience and scope; official PDF copyright page read for rights caveat

title: Guidance on community mental health services: Promoting person-centred and rights-based approaches
summary: WHO guidance describes person-centred community mental-health systems and services aligned with disability rights, choice, autonomy and dignity.
limitations: Policy and service-delivery guidance, not a controlled trial or validation of an automated mental-health companion. Jurisdiction-specific rights and capacity law require separate legal analysis.
rights: Official bibliographic pointer and independent summary only; no source document body redistributed or approved for training.
verification_method: Official WHO normative guidance publication record dated 2021-06-09, overview and ISBN directly verified

title: Eating disorders: recognition and treatment (NG69)
issuer: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
summary: NICE guidance describes recognition, assessment and treatment pathways for eating disorders across children, young people and adults, including coordinated professional care.
limitations: Guideline is for qualified providers, and some eating disorders can involve immediate physical risk. Official guidance was updated 2020-12-16; direct chapter opened with HTTP 403 in this wave, so section-specific claims are not considered independently confirmed.
rights: Bibliographic link and independent general summary only; no full recommendations copied or training rights established.
verification_method: Official NICE indexed recommendation page confirmed ID, original 2017-05-23 publication and 2020-12-16 update; direct chapter retrieval 403
